articles.author: Graeme Wearden
articles.title: Nvidia shares fall in premarket trading as Jensen Huang’s return sparks US political backlash – business live
articles.description: Republicans and Democrats object over Trump’s role in Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO, following an affair with an alleged Chinese spy Democrats hit out at Nvidia and Trump over Huang’s return – US politics live Have you downloaded Meta’s AI assistant Muse or do you plan to? Congress to grill Jensen Huang over ties with China and Trump’s intervention Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia, despite concerns over his conduct and the supply of AI chips to China, may show that AI – and Huang himself – are ‘too big to fail’. That phrase was on everyone’s lips almost 20 years ago when the Global Financial Crisis struck, and several major banks were bailed out. Given Nvidia’s pivotal role in the AI capex rollout, the implications of Huang’s reinstatement could be profound. Borrowing from the GFC, are some technology CEOs now so systemically important to the future of AI and US leadership in the latest technology revolution that they cannot be fired? Questions around the scale of financing required and future monetisation remain, and the dependence on Huang for the future success of AI may paradoxically heighten those concerns especially given Anthropic fell despite yesterday’s broad market rally. “We must investigate these actions. No president who has invested in a private company should be involved in their board decisions. Congress must come together in swift bipartisan action and demand answers immediately.” Continue reading...

articles.title: Outcry grows over UK plan to exempt most brownfield sites from nature protection rules
articles.description: Decision to exempt plots up to 1.5 hectares from biodiversity net gain laws allows developers to dodge rules designed to reverse wildlife declines An outcry is growing over the UK chancellor’s removal of most brownfield housing plots from a legal requirement for developers to measurably enhance nature. John Healey’s decision in the budget to exempt brownfield plots of up to 1.5 hectares from biodiversity net gain (BNG) laws effectively means housing developers of inner-city, urban and surburban sites will be able to dodge rules designed to reverse steep wildlife declines while also allowing housebuilding growth. According to government data, 86% of brownfield sites currently registered are 1.5ha or under. Continue reading...

articles.author: Andrew Cordon
articles.title: Scream 4 came out 15 years ago – but its mockery of online brainrot is more spot-on than ever
articles.description: When Wes Craven’s final slasher film came out, correctly predicting clout-chasing influencers and social media’s corruption of our lives, Instagram was just six months old Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email It has been almost a year since Australia’s social media ban for under-16s and it seems as though nothing has been able to effectively deter the youth from the slippery slope of internet addiction – even when they have expressed the desire to quit . It’s hard to believe that it has only been a decade since TikTok condemned us to the eternal doomscroll and just over 15 years since Instagram launched. Surely no one predicted just how much the online world would be leeching off of us, right? Well, Wes Craven did. Craven is the mind behind notable horror titles including The Hills Have Eyes, A Nightmare on Elm Street and the Scream franchise – and the last film he directed, four years before his death in 2015, was Scream 4. articles.author: Charlotte Jansen
articles.title: What happened when the man who took a million photographs embraced colour?
articles.description: The Photographers’ Gallery, London Sanlé Sory is known for his black and white images taken during independence in Burkina Faso – but his colour portraits bring humour, insouciance and joy Despite his wide renown, there have been hardly any major exhibitions of Sanlé Sory’s work. His last UK show was in 2019, concentrating on the black-and-white images the Burkinabé photographer made in the first two decades after opening his own studio, Volta Photo, in Bobo-Dioulasso in 1960 – a period that coincided with the first two decades of independence in Burkina Faso. This new Photographer’s Gallery show shifts the focus to the 1980s and 1990s, when Sory began working in colour. It’s easy to see why, even with few exhibitions, Sory has made such an impression on audiences. There are the familiar west African studio photography tropes westerners love, where sound, image, fashion and pose collide. The props are popping, the style is irrepressible, the energy is irresistible. I wonder if Sory’s speed and instinct came from the time he spent early in his career racing on his motorbike to photograph car accidents for newspapers and the police. These portraits are the opposite of a car crash, they’re remedially joyful, wilfully alive – but they share that feeling of being inside the moment, at the edge of something. Continue reading...

articles.author: Daniel Wolfe
articles.title: GTA VI’s jaw-dropping success: in figures
articles.description: Content creators have produced hundreds of millions of hours of video game since its launch Grand Theft Auto ( GTA) VI became the largest video game release of all time last week and while it is hard to say exactly how many people are playing the game (current estimates say at least 30 million), there are plenty of other jaw-dropping data points we do know. Data on streaming the game suggests that only two days into its release a cumulative 364.5m hours have been watched – roughly 41,000 years of content. Put another way, that translates to more than 41,000 years worth of people riffling through cash registers, hanging drywall, birding, diving or hijacking jets. That’s according to streaming data from Stream Charts, a data and analytics company that has been tracking Rockstar Game’s long-awaited title. Continue reading...

articles.author: Mark Hendricks
articles.title: Their loss changed Appalachian forests for ever. Now the American chestnut is back
articles.description: The trees have been functionally extinct in the US for nearly a century. But new techniques are creating plants resistant to the parasitic blight that almost wiped them out Jeff White is starstruck by a tree. The farmer and environmentalist from rural Maryland has an affinity with the American chestnut but has never seen one stretch from root to sky like this one. “About how tall is it?” he asks. “Over 70ft [21 metres],” says Cassie Stark, director of science implementation for the American Chestnut Foundation (TACF). “Just incredible,” White says, his gaze fixed upwards. “I’ve never seen one so tall and so healthy.” ‘Thompson’, above left, is an unusually tall specimen of an American chestnut, a now-rare species once ubiquitous in the US. articles.author: Alyssa Mercante
articles.title: Man Theft Auto – why did so few women review GTA VI, the biggest video game of the decade?
articles.description: Given that this is the first Grand Theft Auto in 30 years with a female protagonist, you might have expected to hear from female critics. But you would have expected mostly in vain Grand Theft Auto VI is now the biggest video game launch of all time, and is likely to become the biggest video game of all time. It’s a once-in-a-lifetime event, a phenomenon that will shape games as a medium and pop culture at large for years to come, set against the backdrop of its developers fighting for their rights at studio Rockstar Games . It has snatched sales and streaming records and become the best-reviewed game ever (pulling ahead of 1998’s The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time). It’s also the first GTA game with a female protagonist, who also happens to be a woman of colour. Yet very few women (and seemingly no women of colour) played and reviewed it before release. When GTA IV’s review embargo lifted on 18 November, the gender imbalance was immediately obvious. Out of 156 reviewers, only six appeared to be women. As journalist Lex Luddy noted in a BlueSky post , that is 3.8%. Continue reading...

articles.author: Eduardo Porter
articles.title: Trump, Nvidia and power: could we be nearing the end of tech’s Gilded Age?
articles.description: Oligarchs believe they’re untouchable – the blue wave offers hope that the rampant corruption of the Trump era may soon be over One can imagine high-fives all around Nvidia’s boardroom after the board reinstated Jensen Huang to the CEO suite. The market gave the move a fat thumbs-up, boosting Nvidia’s share price by about a third. Shareholders, whose interests the board is meant to represent, are surely happy. But like Fifa’s controversial decision to defer the one-match suspension of US forward Folarin Balogun after receiving a red card for a foul on Bosnia and Herzegovina’s Tarik Muharemović during the World Cup over the summer, Huang’s absolution might backfire. Eduardo Porter is a journalist focused on economics and politics. He writes the newsletter Being There on Substack Continue reading...

articles.title: Meta launches Muse in UK – the AI agent that can do your Christmas shopping
articles.description: Users can give agents tasks such as booking travel or buying presents, but glitches have been reported Have you downloaded Meta’s AI assistant Muse or do you plan to? Want to avoid the Christmas shopping hordes? Then let your AI agent do it. Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta is launching its Muse AI assistant in the UK and is encouraging users to let it loose on their apps – and the high street. Muse has been a hit in the US and is ranked first and second respectively on Google and Apple’s free app store, having been downloaded millions of times. Continue reading...

articles.author: Josh Butler
articles.title: Kate Bush and Grace Jones urge Australian government not to legalise AI ‘theft’
articles.description: Singers among 7,000 artists and creatives urging Labor to protect copyright law in face of lobbying from AI companies Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Kate Bush, Grace Jones and Sir Ian Rankin have joined 7,000 artists and creatives around the world pleading for the Australian government not to weaken copyright law, urging Labor not to “not legalise the theft of the work of the world’s creators on their soil”. The international push, the latest in a global pushback against artificial intelligence companies and their requests to water down copyright, comes the same day a long-awaited parliamentary committee handed down a mammoth report calling for copyright reform in Australia. Continue reading...

articles.author: Dara Kerr
articles.title: Nvidia rejoices at Jensen Huang’s second coming as White House takes victory lap
articles.description: Huang receives hero’s welcome at firm’s Silicon Valley headquarters as return cements role as key AI figure Comment: Nvidia’s humiliated board should resign out of embarrassment Business live – latest updates Jensen Huang made his return to Nvidia’s headquarters with a hero’s welcome on Monday. Hours earlier he’d been reinstated as the CEO of the world’s most valuable chip company, following a whiplash series of events that involved a romantic affair with a suspected Chinese spy, a drastic plummet in the stock market, and an intervention from Donald Trump. As Huang entered the company’s Silicon Valley office, wearing his signature dark-colored uniform, crowds of employees rushed to greet him clapping, hollering and chanting: “Jensen, Jensen, Jensen!” Continue reading...
